## Overdispersion

**Overdispersion** occurs when the response variable $Y_i$ has greater variability than the model accounts for.

\vspace{1cm}

**Poisson:** $Var(Y_i | \mathbf{x}_i) = \mathbb{E}[Y_i | \mathbf{x}_i] = \mu_i$

\vspace{2cm}


## Negative Binomial models

$$Y \sim NB(\mu, r) \hspace{1cm} f(y; \mu, r) = \frac{\Gamma(y + r)}{\Gamma(y + 1)\Gamma(r)} \left(\frac{\mu}{\mu + r} \right)^y \left(1 - \frac{\mu}{\mu + r} \right)^r$$

$$Y_i | \mathbf{x}_i \sim NB(\mu_i, r) \hspace{1cm} \log(\mu_i) = \mathbf{x}_i^T \boldsymbol{\beta}$$

\vspace{6cm}

## Example: articles data

```{r}
m3 <- MASS::glm.nb(art ~ phd + ment + kid5, data = articles)
```

```
             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
(Intercept)  0.233528   0.117585   1.986   0.0470 *  
phd          0.008203   0.036069   0.227   0.8201    
ment         0.030374   0.003240   9.373   <2e-16 ***
kid5        -0.093256   0.046475  -2.007   0.0448 *  

(Dispersion parameter for Negative Binomial(2.1647) 
   family taken to be 1)

AIC: 3145.6
```

## Inference for negative binomial models

* Can use the usual Wald tests for $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ (from asymptotic normality)
* LRT also works because a full distribution is specified

\vspace{7cm}

## Example: articles data

```{r}
m3 <- MASS::glm.nb(art ~ phd + ment + kid5, data = articles)
m4 <- MASS::glm.nb(art ~ phd + kid5, data = articles)

pchisq(m3$twologlik - m4$twologlik, 1, lower.tail=F)
```

\vspace{4cm}

## New data

Survey data from 77 college students on a dry campus (i.e., alcohol is prohibited) in the US. Survey asks students "How many alcoholic drinks did you consume last weekend?"

* `drinks`: number of drinks the student reports consuming
* `sex`: whether the student identifies as male
* `OffCampus`: whether the student lives off campus
* `FirstYear`: whether the student is a first-year student

Our goal: model the number of drinks students report consuming.

## EDA: drinks

```{r echo=F, message=F, warning=F, fig.align='center', fig.width=4, fig.height=3}
library(tidyverse)

wdrinks <- read.csv("../class_activities/weekendDrinks.csv")

FirstYear <- ifelse( wdrinks$dorm %in% c("mohn","kittlesby", "kildahl"), "TRUE", "FALSE")
OffCampus <- ifelse( wdrinks$dorm == "off campus", "TRUE", "FALSE")

wdrinks <- cbind(wdrinks, FirstYear, OffCampus)

wdrinks %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = drinks)) +
  geom_bar() +
  theme_bw()
```

What do you notice about this distribution?

## Comparisons with Poisson distributions

```{r echo=F, message=F, warning=F, fig.align='center', fig.width=4, fig.height=3.5}
library(gridExtra)
set.seed(1)
p1 <- wdrinks %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = drinks)) +
  geom_bar() +
  theme_bw() +
  #theme(text = element_text(size = 25)) +
  labs(title = "Observed data", x = "", y = "") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 25)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 45))

p2 <- data.frame(x = rpois(100, 1)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x)) +
  geom_bar() +
  theme_bw() +
  #theme(text = element_text(size = 25)) +
  labs(title = "Poisson(1)", x = "", y = "") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 25)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 45))

p3 <- data.frame(x = rpois(100, 2)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x)) +
  geom_bar() +
  theme_bw() +
  #theme(text = element_text(size = 25)) +
  labs(title = "Poisson(2)", x = "", y = "") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 25)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 45))

p4 <- data.frame(x = rpois(100, 5)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x)) +
  geom_bar() +
  theme_bw() +
  #theme(text = element_text(size = 25)) +
  labs(title = "Poisson(5)", x = "", y = "") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 25)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 45))

grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, p4, ncol=2)
```

## Excess zeros

*Why might there be excess 0s in the data, and why is that a problem for modeling the number of drinks consumed?*

```{r echo=F, message=F, warning=F, fig.align='center', fig.width=3, fig.height=2.5}
wdrinks %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = drinks)) +
  geom_bar() +
  theme_bw()
```

## Zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP) model

## In R

```{r message=F, warning=F}
library(pscl)

m1 <- zeroinfl(drinks ~ sex + FirstYear + OffCampus, 
               dist = "poisson", data = wdrinks)

m1$coefficients
```
